notes: Every check cites official CyberArk (Idira) documentation on docs.cyberark.com.

The 'find' text is a phrase to Ctrl+F on the cited page. It was taken from search-index excerpts because direct page fetch was blocked when this catalog was built. Re-verify each one on the live page before relying on it.

confidence: Documented = the doc states the setting and value. StepDocumented-MechanismInferred = the doc states the step, but the registry key, service name or probe used to verify it comes from Windows knowledge, not the doc. VersionDependent = the docs differ between versions.

checks.title: PSMHardening.ps1 has run and its log has no errors
checks.remediation: Run <PSM>\Hardening\PSMHardening.ps1 as Administrator (execution policy RemoteSigned, read-only flag removed). Then review the log.

checklist.expected: Exists; no lines with Error / Failed / Exception
checklist.note: The log file name and location are inferred; the doc says only 'check the log for errors'.

checks.title: Hardening re-applied after the last PSM upgrade
checks.remediation: After an upgrade, re-run the NEW PSMHardening.ps1 and PSMConfigureAppLocker.ps1. Do not use the backed-up copies.

checklist.expected: Newest hardening log is newer than newest PSM binary (hardening re-run after upgrade)

checks.title: RDP-Tcp MinEncryptionLevel = 3 (High)
checks.remediation: Re-run PSMHardening.ps1, or set MinEncryptionLevel=3 on the RDP-Tcp listener.

checklist.note: Value from the CyberArk doc; key location is standard Windows.

checks.title: RDP-Tcp SecurityLayer changed by hardening (review the value)
checks.remediation: The docs say the script changes SecurityLayer but the excerpt did not give the target value. Compare against the PSM hardening page for your version.

checklist.expected: Value set by PSMHardening.ps1. Windows meaning: 0 = RDP, 1 = Negotiate, 2 = SSL/TLS. Target value not confirmed from the doc.

checklist.location: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Security

checks.remediation: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false, or re-run hardening.

checks.title: Entra ID joined server with the RDS Session Host role installed (field-reported Entra SSO / logon breakage)
checks.remediation: PSM needs the RDS Session Host role, so on an Entra-joined PSM host test Entra/SSO logon after role install and after hardening. Microsoft Learn does not state this break for standalone RDS (AVD documents Entra-joined session hosts WITH this role), so treat as a field-reported risk and validate in your build.

checklist.expected: If Entra joined: flag as RISK and test Entra / SSO logon
Document the join type; Microsoft goal state for Entra logon: AzureAdJoined : YES, AzureAdPrt : YES
